doc_friction.issue: The Leidenfrost proposal said the failed first try was the agent 'lowering the setting because the drops lasted', which contradicts its own premise (a rule of 'lasting means cool' raises the setting); cost a few minutes working out which the proposer meant.

The proposal's suggested source, a translation of Leidenfrost's tract, could not be confirmed (venue and year conflict between sources), so the note cites the 1756 tract and Walker's retelling instead; proposals should only name sources they have checked.

deviations.why: Proposal had the agent lower the setting; physically, misreading a long-lived drop as a cool plate makes it raise it.
deviations.did: Agent raises 9 to 12 (wrong-sign feedback runs the plate hot); said so in DONE.md, the PR and the post.
deviations.result: Story's failure is consistent with its note's model.

certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
